record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.original_question: Can a low-energy beta-beam facility, either at a future exotic-ion laboratory such as GSI, GANIL, EURISOL, or RIA or as part of the high-energy CERN beta-beam facility, meet the essential requirements of attainable ion intensity and an available storage ring for ions?

evidence.quote: Two possible scenarios can be envisaged for a low-energy beta-beam facility [28] where it is part either of one of the future nuclear laboratories (or projects) for the production very intense exotic ion beams (like e.g. GSI, GANIL, EURISOL or RIA), or of the high energy beta-beam facility at CERN.
For the former case, there are several requirements which should be met. Two essential aspects are the ion intensity which can be attained and the availability of a ring to store the ions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the proposal of a low-energy beta-beam facility, in which radioactive ions that undergo beta decay are produced, accelerated to (relatively low) Lorentz boost factors, and stored in a circulating ring so that the resulting pure (anti-)electron-neutrino beam emerging from beta decay can be directed toward a low-energy neutrino-nucleus experiment. Two architectural scenarios are envisaged:

(a) the facility is embedded in a dedicated exotic-ion laboratory (such as a high-intensity radioactive ion beam facility of GSI/GANIL/EURISOL/RIA type), or

(b) the facility is appended to a high-energy beta-beam complex at a large hadron laboratory (CERN-type), with an additional low-energy storage ring downstream.

For either scenario, the two essential technical requirements are:
(i) the attainable production intensity of suitable beta-unstable ions (e.g., 6He, 18Ne) must be sufficient to yield a useful neutrino flux at the detector; and
(ii) a storage ring capable of accumulating and circulating these ions at the desired (low) gamma factor must be available.

Problem: Determine whether either of the scenarios (a) or (b) can simultaneously meet requirements (i) and (ii) at a level sufficient to make a low-energy beta-beam facility feasible for neutrino-nucleus interaction studies.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent design studies (EURISOL Design Study under FP6, beta-beam Letter of Intent, and HIE-ISOLDE storage ring technical design report) have continued to investigate the feasibility of a low-energy beta-beam, addressing both ion intensity targets and storage ring concepts. However, no low-energy beta-beam facility has been built, and the question of whether the required ion intensities and a dedicated storage ring can be realized in practice remains an open feasibility/design question rather than a settled result.

status_evidence.title: Letter of Intent: FP6 Design Study for a beta-beam facility
status_evidence.snippet: A feasibility study into the use of the EURISOL facility for the production of pure electron-neutrinos is an integral part of design study; this is the so-called new 'beta-beam' proposal.
status_evidence.claim: Feasibility of a beta-beam facility based on EURISOL was still under study, not demonstrated.

status_evidence.title: A low energy storage ring for partly stripped radioactive ions
status_evidence.snippet: Design proposal for a low-energy storage ring suitable for radioactive ions.
status_evidence.claim: Low-energy storage rings for radioactive ions remain at design-study stage.

status_evidence.title: Storage ring facility at HIE-ISOLDE: Technical Design Report
status_evidence.snippet: Technical design report for a storage ring at HIE-ISOLDE.
status_evidence.claim: Storage-ring component for radioactive ions is the subject of ongoing technical design rather than completed construction.

status_evidence.title: Eurisol - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: EURISOL is conceived as a next-generation European ISOL radioactive ion beam facility; the project has progressed through feasibility and design studies.
status_evidence.claim: Host facility for a low-energy beta-beam has not been constructed; the project is in design-study phase.
